scope: Balance the shared GTK private-text lifecycle without publication or foreign selection ownership changes. All five complete desktop editions and installed editor/helper composition remain open.
settings_fixture_repair: Successful settings behavior checks retained gtk_main_quit criticals after its loop had returned. The destructor signal callback now quits only a live loop. The observer enables fatal criticals and explicitly rejects GTK warnings/criticals. Original behavior-pass records remain superseded diagnostic evidence, not clean shutdown qualification.
workspace_stop: A configure preflight stopped at the unchanged 8 GiB ceiling after native package copies. Archive verification preceded removal of the duplicate frontend attempt; subsequent preflight passed. No quota or standard reservation was increased.
diagnosis: Original shared control removed GTK PRIMARY registration during realization, then GTK removed it again during unrealize. The fatal-critical consumer reproduces native exit -5. Lifecycle wrappers restore only the reference immediately before synchronous parent consumption; destroy unrealizes before parent buffer replacement.
oracle_notes: The test consumer hide/unrealize/show cycle now remaps the control. Subsequent child launches disable core dumps to bound intentional fatal-diagnostic testing; fatal criticals and expected outcomes remain unchanged. Foreign ownership calibration detects two transfers even after owner restoration.

preservation.runtime_roots: F base and historical crash orphans retained; no source or build artifact deleted.

limitations: Pinned Linux GTK 3.24.41 ext4/Xvfb/AT-SPI lab only; no Wayland, other GTK version or complete accessibility qualification.
Private control owns its buffer; buffer replacement/sharing and external registration mutation are outside its caller contract.
Windows component graphs regenerated; no Windows UI code changed and no historical guest execution claimed.
No protected-policy deployment or release publication.
next_step: Integrate the native editor/inspector into the installed frontend, with worker-owned verified image/recovery helper launches, live telemetry, activation and independent desktop recovery.
